conf.description: z/OS ACF2/Top Secret logon-events, syslog-raw: branches on record shape (no-pipe => Top Secret EARLOUT fixed byte positions per work order; pipe-delimited => ACF2 zSecure/CDP unload). Per recommendations.direct.cribl: derive event.reason from RC via lookup, event.outcome from the L flag / TSS return code.

conf.comment: logon-events / syslog-raw. Two products share this feed: Top Secret EARLOUT (fixed byte positions given in the work order: ACID NAME 14-21, TERMINAL ID 54-61, FACILITY NAME 70-77, RETURN CODE 82-83, DETAIL REASON CODE 84-86, SYSID 111-114 - extracted verbatim) and ACF2 (only column NAMES are published, not byte offsets, so this pipeline targets the pipe-delimited zSecure/CDP unload variant the work order also describes, in the field table's documented order). Branch discriminator is presence of '|' - a heuristic, not a documented discriminator field; both the discriminator and the ACF2 column order are unverified against a captured sample. See README.

functions.description: Top Secret EARLOUT branch: fixed byte positions taken verbatim from the work order.

ACF2 branch: pipe-delimited zSecure/CDP unload (record descriptor + DATE + TIME prefix, then named columns in the work order's documented field order). Column order is inferred, not confirmed against a real unload sample.

add.name: event.reason
add.value: __e['RC'] === '4' ? 'logonid does not exist' : (__e['RC'] === '11' || __e['RC'] === '13') ? 'suspended or cancelled' : __e['RC'] === '12' ? 'invalid password' : __e['RC'] === '17' ? 'expired password' : undefined

functions.description: RC -> event.code + event.reason via the RC values the recommendation enumerates (4/11/13/12/17 only - 'plus shift/source and authorization ranges' is not itemized anywhere, so those stay unresolved, a documented gap); event.outcome from the ACF2 L flag or, on the Top Secret branch, from RETURN CODE. Computed before the rename step below, straight off the raw column names.

Batch-rename every straight-copy status:mapped/partial/unmapped field (no computed transform, and not read again downstream) to its ECS or custom target. ACF2 and Top Secret both land on user.name/source.address/host.name so one rule covers the estate.

Fallback event time. DATE+TIME->UTC needs a Julian/packed-date conversion plus an LPAR timezone offset keyed on CPU/SYSID that recommendations.direct.cribl calls for but supplies no lookup table for - documented gap, not implemented. auto_timestamp's own heuristic against _raw is used instead.

Tag event.category from the dataset's own event_categories; event.action 'logon' for the ACF2 branch (every record in this dataset is a system-entry attempt by definition - RECORD TYPE IN/TR would give the Top Secret equivalent but its byte position isn't documented, so it's left unset there, a gap). Re-uses the '|' branch discriminator on _raw (still intact this late in the pipeline, unlike LID which the earlier rename step already retargeted to user.name) rather than testing a field the rename step consumed. event.dataset set to the data stream's own dataset component (logs-zos_acf2.logon_events), not a generic tech.dataset string.
